entry.source: עָזִּי וְזִמְרָת יָהּ וַיְהִי־לִי לִישׁוּעָה (Exod 15:2; Ps 118:14; Isa 12:2, with יְהוָה added after יָהּ)
entry.strongs: H5797 (ʿōz); H2176 (zimrāṯ); H3050 (Yāh); H3444 (yᵉšûʿāh). Numbers from recall, not concordance-verified.
entry.lemma: the Song of the Sea confession 'my strength and my song is Yah', with zimrāh 'song' vs zimrāh 'protection, might'
entry.partOfSpeech: nominal clause (two nouns, the second without its own suffix) + wayyiqtol clause
entry.literal: my strength and song (of?) Yah, and he became for me for salvation
entry.standardEnglish: ASV 'Jehovah is my strength and song, And he is become my salvation' (Exod 15:2; Ps 118:14; Isa 12:2 'Jehovah, [even] Jehovah'); JPS 1917 'my strength and song'; NJPS 'my strength and might' (Isa 12:2, checked on Sefaria, with a note giving 'song' as the alternative); NRSV 'my strength and my might' (recalled, not verified)
entry.wohChoice: '[Yah] is my strength and my song, and he has become my salvation' as the English wording for the shared line, fixed for Isaiah and proposed as the default for the other books: Isa 12:2 'for Yah YHWH is my strength and my song, and he has become my salvation'; Exod 15:2 and Ps 118:14 'Yah is my strength and my song, and he has become my salvation' (forward-scope DEFAULT, to be confirmed by those books' Editors, pending founder ruling). zimrāh I 'song' is kept, with zimrāh II 'protection, might' recorded in commentary at each site. 'my' is supplied on both nouns. Yāh is transliterated 'Yah' and kept distinct from 'YHWH' (Isaiah overlay yah-tzur-olamim-everlasting-rock-isaiah-26). Where a book has the doubled name (Isa 12:2), the line follows that book's MT.
entry.rationale: The confession ʿozzî wᵉzimrāṯ Yāh wayᵉhî-lî lîšûʿāh is quoted word for word in three books: the Song of the Sea (Exod 15:2), the thanksgiving of Ps 118 (118:14), and the hymn closing Isa 1-12 (12:2, which adds YHWH after Yāh). One wording is needed so the quotation can be seen across the corpus, as the Isa 2:2-4 // Mic 4:1-3 parallel entry does for that pair. The crux is zimrāṯ. It lacks the first-person suffix, which is usually explained as an archaic feminine ending or as -î lost before Yāh, so 'my' is supplied on both nouns. Its meaning is disputed. BDB takes it from zmr I 'sing, make music' ('song'), while HALOT lists a second zimrāh 'protection, strength', connected with Ugaritic ḏmr. NJPS's 'might' (and, as recalled, NRSV's) follows the second view. The Editor keeps 'song', the reading of the public-domain baseline (ASV, JPS 1917) and of the older Jewish and Christian English tradition. The 'might' reading is a serious lexical alternative, not an error, so it is disclosed at every site rather than suppressed. Isaiah-specific support only: in Isa 12 the 'song' reading also fits the immediate context (zammᵉrû 'sing praises', 12:5). That argument does not carry to Exod 15:2 or Ps 118:14, and the Editors of those books must weigh zimrāh in their own contexts. wayᵉhî-lî lîšûʿāh is rendered 'and he has become my salvation' (ASV 'is become', modernized). The choice is a standard rendering and carries no lens, so the claim is direct. Forward scope is a DEFAULT, pending a founder ruling. When exodus-woh 15 and psalms-woh 118 are drafted, their Editors should confirm this wording for EXO-15:2 and PSA-118:14, or escalate a departure, before those refIds are added to appliesTo.

rationaleAppend: Prophetic extension (Isaiah wave I-3): the imperative with suffix qirʾû ḇišmô 'call on his name' at Isa 12:4, in the hymn that repeats Ps 105:1 = 1 Chr 16:8, is rendered with the formula's corpus verb 'call on'. JPS 1917 and NJPS read 'proclaim his name' there, the sense qārāʾ bᵉšēm has at Exod 34:5. That alternative is recorded in the Isaiah commentary.
